WFCvkkDSfIU.title: Animations of unseeable biology | Drew Berry | TED
WFCvkkDSfIU.summary: Drew Berry shows scientifically accurate animations of molecular processes inside cells, such as DNA replication, at TEDxSydney.
WFCvkkDSfIU.why: HN recommends it for mind-blowing visuals that make cell biology tangible.

quote.text: I had a much greater appreciation for how our bodies are made up of trillions of tiny protein machines.

1-dUkyn_fZA.title: Emacs + org-mode + python in reproducible research; SciPy 2013 Presentation
1-dUkyn_fZA.summary: John Kitchin shows how Emacs org-mode with Python lets researchers combine narrative, math, figures and executable code in one document. It exports to LaTeX, HTML and PDF, and he used it for papers and e-books.
1-dUkyn_fZA.why: Repeatedly recommended as the canonical demo of org-mode for literate programming and reproducible research.

quote.text: on Emacs + org-mode + python in reproducible research is worth a watch

VQKMoT-6XSg.title: iPhone 1 - Steve Jobs MacWorld keynote in 2007 - Full Presentation, 80 mins

VQKMoT-6XSg.why: Cited as a landmark tech presentation, especially for the audience's astonished reaction to touch scrolling and demo moments like visual voicemail.

quote.text: I consider AlphaGo - The Movie [1] to be a timeless classic that will never feel outdated.

2IT2oAzTcvU.title: Nina Kollars - Confessions of an Nespresso Money Mule - DEF CON 27 Conference
2IT2oAzTcvU.summary: At DEF CON 27, Nina Kollars tells how buying Nespresso capsules on eBay led her to investigate fraudsters reselling goods bought with stolen credit cards. She describes her non-technical tracking and reporting efforts.
2IT2oAzTcvU.why: HN points to it as an entertaining and informative explanation of the economics of reshipping and stolen-card resale scams.

quote.text: here's an excellent defcon talk on what these some groups do

KqFNbCcyFkk.title: The Fall of The Simpsons: How it Happened
KqFNbCcyFkk.summary: Super Eyepatch Wolf analyzes why The Simpsons declined after its golden age, pointing to changes in the writers' room and a shift in the style and complexity of its comedy.
KqFNbCcyFkk.why: HN treats it as the definitive explanation of the Simpsons decline, recommended in every thread asking when the golden age ended.

quote.text: For an actual exploration of what happened, I highly recommend this video.

SC2eSujzrUY.title: The Biggest Chemical Coverup In History
SC2eSujzrUY.summary: Veritasium investigates PFAS forever chemicals, from Teflon's history to pollution of the global water system and their presence in the US population. It covers the corporate cover-up and the host's own blood tests.
SC2eSujzrUY.why: Recommended as a good, accessible explanation of PFAS, its low safe limits and why regulation matters.

quote.text: If you want a good explanation of PFAs, Veritasium did a video on it.

H62hZJVqs2o.title: "Uptime 15,364 days - The Computers of Voyager" by Aaron Cummings
H62hZJVqs2o.summary: A Strange Loop 2019 talk by Aaron Cummings on the computing systems aboard Voyager 1 and 2, which control the spacecraft and record and return data decades after launch in 1977.
H62hZJVqs2o.why: HN recommends it in Voyager threads as a good talk on how these old computers have proved durable and adaptable.

quote.text: this talk was really good

PtKhbbcc1Rc.title: Does "land area" assume a country is perfectly flat?
PtKhbbcc1Rc.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths asks whether a country's reported land area accounts for hills and mountains, working through how surface area depends on the resolution of elevation data. It follows up on a question from a viewer and work by researchers who measured it.
PtKhbbcc1Rc.why: HN recommends it in map projection and coastline threads as a fun look at how measurement choices change area figures.

quote.text: Matt Parker from Standup Maths made a great video on exactly this subject

X9RYuvPCQUA.title: Everything is a Remix (2023 Edition)
X9RYuvPCQUA.summary: Kirby Ferguson's updated four-part video essay arguing that creativity is built on copying, transforming and combining existing work. It covers examples from film, music and technology and touches on generative AI.
X9RYuvPCQUA.why: Pointed to in copyright and AI debates as a compelling case that all culture is remix.

quote.text: It highlights how essentially everything in culture is a remix of some previous version of the culture

QLUIExAnNcE.title: Understanding the Honda CR-V Hybrid E-Drive
QLUIExAnNcE.summary: WeberAuto explains how the Honda E-Drive (i-MMD) hybrid transaxle works in the CR-V, Accord, Insight and Clarity hybrids. It walks through the system's three modes of operation.
QLUIExAnNcE.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of a mind-blowingly simple power-split hybrid design.

J7GY1Xg6X20.title: Charlie Chaplin - Final Speech from The Great Dictator
J7GY1Xg6X20.summary: The closing speech from Charlie Chaplin's 1940 film The Great Dictator, in which the barber appeals for humanity, kindness and liberty over machinery and cleverness.

OTVE5iPMKLg.title: Your Coffee Addiction Is Probably Good for You

zp0OEDcAro0.title: Condition Systems in an Exceptional Language - Chris Houser
zp0OEDcAro0.summary: Chris Houser's Clojure/conj talk on why Clojure's exceptions destroy information as the stack unwinds, unlike Common Lisp's condition system, which can resume from the error site. He surveys the existing libraries that approximate conditions, explains why they don't compose with each other, and considers what a better design would look like.
zp0OEDcAro0.why: Clojure commenters cite it as the best overview of condition systems in Clojure and of the libraries that attempt them.

quote.text: A great overview of the problem and some of the libs is
